answer: One concrete Sybil defense is slashable identity bonds. Before an agent's vote counts, it must lock collateral in a public on-ledger registry, and peers check that every name carries its own bond. To forge a thousand fake voters, an attacker must post a thousand equal bonds, so the cost of influence grows linearly with the number of identities. Any double-vote or reused key slashes the whole stake. Honest agents form an orchard that guards a shared haven of locked value; the attacker must forge one fresh bond per vote until the bill far exceeds anything one rigged outcome could pay.
